blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Chapter 6 (Emerging Technologies), arranged by the chapter's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each answer is a short model answer; small numericals show the working, and a comparison is answered as a table.
6.1 Definition and Overview of Emerging Technologies

blocks.prompt: 1 Define emerging technologies. Name any two of them.
blocks.explanation: Emerging technologies are new tools, systems and methods that are currently being developed or have just started to be used; they can change the way we live, work and interact with the world. Examples: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Blockchain.

book_ref.quote: These technologies have the potential to change the way we live, work, and interact with the world

blocks.prompt: 2 What is Artificial Intelligence? Give two tasks it can help with.
blocks.explanation: AI refers to machines and software that can think and learn like humans. It can help with tasks like recognizing faces and understanding speech (also making decisions), e.g. in Siri and self-driving cars.

book_ref.quote: AI can help with tasks like recognizing faces, understanding speech, and making decisions

blocks.prompt: 3 Differentiate between Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR).
blocks.explanation: AR mixes digital elements into the real world; VR replaces it with a fully virtual one.

book_ref.quote: VR creates a completely virtual environment that you can interact with using special equipment

rows: Adds digital elements to the real world
Creates a completely virtual environment
Uses devices like smartphones or glasses
Uses special equipment to interact with it
Used in gaming, education and training
Used in gaming, education and training

blocks.prompt: 4 What is the Internet of Things (IoT)? Give one example.
blocks.explanation: IoT connects everyday objects, like refrigerators, cars and even clothes, to the internet so that they can send and receive data. Example: a smart thermostat learns your schedule and adjusts the home temperature automatically.

book_ref.quote: IoT connects everyday objects, like refrigerators, cars, and even clothes, to the internet

blocks.prompt: 5 What is quantum computing?
blocks.explanation: Quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process information much faster than traditional computers. They have the potential to solve very complex problems that are currently impossible for regular computers.

book_ref.quote: They have the potential to solve very complex problems that are currently impossible for regular computers

blocks.prompt: 6 What is biotechnology? Give two of its uses.
blocks.explanation: Biotechnology involves using living organisms, like bacteria and plants, to create new products or solve problems. Uses: developing new medicines and improving crops (also environmentally friendly materials).

book_ref.quote: scientists are using biotechnology to develop new medicines, improve crops

blocks.prompt: 7 What is 5G technology? What will it enable?
blocks.explanation: 5G is the next generation of wireless technology, offering much faster internet speeds and more reliable connections. It will enable better performance for mobile phones, smart devices and new technologies like AR and VR.

book_ref.quote: This will enable better performance for mobile phones, smart devices

blocks.prompt: 8 Define cloud computing.
blocks.explanation: Cloud computing is a model that allows easy and convenient access to computing resources like servers, storage and applications over the internet. These resources can be quickly provided and released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction.

book_ref.quote: These resources can be quickly provided and released with minimal management effort

blocks.prompt: 9 Give a reason: cloud computing makes it easier and cheaper to get things done.
blocks.explanation: Instead of buying and maintaining your own expensive computers and storage devices, you use cloud services over the internet. You can use as much or as little of the service as you need and you only pay for what you use.

book_ref.quote: Instead of buying and maintaining your own expensive computers and storage devices

blocks.prompt: 10 What is virtualization? Write two of its benefits.
blocks.explanation: Virtualization is a technology that allows a single physical machine to run multiple virtual machines, each with its own operating system and applications. Benefits: better use of the hardware and reduced costs (also easier management and flexibility).

book_ref.quote: It's like turning one computer into many, making it possible to do more with less

blocks.prompt: 11 Define scalability with an example.
blocks.explanation: Scalability means you can add more resources when you need them. Example: an online store gets a huge spike in traffic during Eid or 14th August sales; it adds more servers so the website runs smoothly without slowing down or crashing.

book_ref.quote: you can add more servers to handle this increased traffic

blocks.prompt: 12 Differentiate between scalability and elasticity.
blocks.explanation: Elasticity takes scalability a step further by making the adjustment automatic.

book_ref.quote: This automatic adjustment helps keep your website running efficiently and cost-effectively

rows: You can add more resources when you need them
The system automatically adjusts resources based on current demand
Example: adding more servers for Eid sale traffic
Example: servers added automatically when traffic rises and reduced after the sale
Resources are added when you need them
Resources are also reduced when demand falls, so you don't pay for what you don't need

blocks.prompt: 13 What is on-demand access? Give the book's analogy.
blocks.explanation: On-demand access means that you can use computing resources whenever you need them, without waiting for a long setup process. It is like turning on a tap to get water whenever you want, instead of having to dig a well first.

book_ref.quote: without waiting for a long setup process

blocks.prompt: 14 Name the three main types of cloud services.
blocks.explanation:
1. Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
2. Platform as a Service (PaaS)
3. Software as a Service (SaaS)
Each offers different levels of control, flexibility and management.

book_ref.quote: Each type offers different levels of control, flexibility, and management

blocks.prompt: 15 What is IaaS? What does the user control in it?
blocks.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) offers basic computing infrastructure such as servers, storage and networking on a pay-as-you-go basis. Users control the operating systems, applications and storage, but not the underlying physical infrastructure.

book_ref.quote: Users have control over the operating systems, applications, and storage, but not the underlying physical infrastructure

blocks.prompt: 16 Name any three IaaS providers.
blocks.explanation:
1. Amazon Web Services (AWS), which lets users rent virtual servers
2. Microsoft Azure
3. Google Compute Engine

book_ref.quote: Amazon Web Services (AWS) allows users to rent virtual servers to run their applications

blocks.prompt: 17 What is PaaS? Give two examples.
blocks.explanation: PaaS (Platform as a Service) offers a complete development and deployment environment in the cloud: infrastructure, middleware, development tools and management services. Developers focus on coding without managing hardware and software layers. Examples: Google App Engine, Heroku.

book_ref.quote: Developers can focus on coding and deploying applications without managing the hardware and software layers

blocks.prompt: 18 What is SaaS? Give two examples.
blocks.explanation: SaaS (Software as a Service) provides access to software applications hosted and managed by the service provider; users simply subscribe and use them over the internet. Examples: Google Workspace (Gmail, Google Docs, Google Drive) and Microsoft Office 365.

book_ref.quote: SaaS provides access to software applications that are hosted and managed by the service provider

blocks.prompt: 19 Differentiate between IaaS and SaaS.
blocks.explanation: IaaS gives infrastructure that the user manages from the operating system upward; SaaS gives ready software.

book_ref.quote: Other examples are Microsoft Office 365 and Salesforce

rows: Offers basic computing infrastructure: servers, storage, networking
Offers software applications hosted and managed by the provider
User controls operating systems, applications and storage
User simply subscribes and uses the software over the internet
Example: AWS virtual servers, Google Compute Engine
Example: Google Workspace, Microsoft Office 365, Salesforce

blocks.prompt: 20 What is the pay-as-you-go model of cloud computing?
blocks.explanation: Cloud computing services are priced based on usage: you pay only for what you use. This pay-as-you-go model lets businesses scale their resources according to their needs, making it cost-effective and flexible.

book_ref.quote: This pay-as-you-go model allows businesses to scale their resources according to their needs

blocks.prompt: 21 What is Salesforce known for? How does it help businesses?
blocks.explanation: Salesforce is a leading SaaS provider known for its customer relationship management (CRM) platform. It helps businesses manage customer data, track sales and automate marketing tasks.

book_ref.quote: It helps businesses manage customer data, track sales, and automate marketing tasks

blocks.prompt: 22 What are cloud deployment models? Name them.
blocks.explanation: Cloud deployment models define how cloud services are made available and used; each offers different levels of control, security and flexibility. The main models are Public, Private, Hybrid and Multi-Cloud.

book_ref.quote: Each model offers different levels of control, security, and flexibility

blocks.prompt: 23 What is a public cloud? Give an example.
blocks.explanation: A public cloud is a cloud service offered over the internet that is shared among multiple organizations and managed by a third-party cloud service provider. Example: Amazon Web Services (AWS), which businesses of all sizes use without managing physical hardware.

book_ref.quote: Businesses of all sizes can use AWS to access computing resources like virtual servers and storage

blocks.prompt: 24 What is a private cloud? Why may a large bank use it?
blocks.explanation: A private cloud is a cloud environment used exclusively by one organization; it may be hosted on-premises or by a third party but is not shared. A large bank may use it to handle sensitive customer data securely, since only the bank has access to it.

book_ref.quote: This private cloud can be hosted within the bank's own data centers

blocks.prompt: 25 Differentiate between a public cloud and a private cloud.
blocks.explanation: The public cloud is shared and cheaper; the private cloud belongs to one organization and is more secure.

book_ref.quote: A private cloud is a cloud environment used exclusively by one organization

rows: Shared among multiple organizations over the internet
Used exclusively by one organization
Managed by a third-party cloud service provider
Hosted on-premises or by a third-party provider
Cost-effective but less secure
More secure but expensive
Example: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
Example: a large bank's cloud for sensitive customer data

blocks.prompt: 26 What is a hybrid cloud? Give an example.
blocks.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines public and private clouds, allowing data and applications to be shared between them; it gives greater flexibility and control. Example: a company uses a public cloud for everyday operations and a private cloud for sensitive data.

book_ref.quote: This model provides greater flexibility and control

blocks.prompt: 27 What is multi-cloud? Why is it used?
blocks.explanation: A multi-cloud approach uses multiple cloud services from different providers. It avoids dependency on a single provider and can enhance reliability and performance: if one provider has issues, the company can still rely on the others.

book_ref.quote: This ensures that if one provider experiences issues, the company can still rely on other services

blocks.prompt: 28 Differentiate between a hybrid cloud and a multi-cloud.
blocks.explanation: A hybrid cloud mixes public and private clouds; a multi-cloud mixes providers.

book_ref.quote: A multi-cloud approach uses multiple cloud services from different providers

rows: Combines public and private clouds
Uses multiple cloud services from different providers
Data and applications are shared between the public and private parts
Different tasks go to different providers
Offers flexibility and control
Provides resilience; avoids dependency on one provider
Example: public cloud for everyday work, private cloud for sensitive data
Example: Google Cloud for analytics, Azure for enterprise apps, AWS for backup

blocks.prompt: 29 Compare the four cloud deployment models in one line each.
blocks.explanation: Each deployment model has its own advantages and disadvantages, depending on the needs and goals of the organization.

book_ref.quote: Each cloud deployment model has its own advantages and disadvantages

rows: Public cloud
Cost-effective but less secure
Private cloud
More secure but expensive
Hybrid cloud

Multi-cloud
Provides resilience

blocks.prompt: 30 What is cloud storage? Name two cloud storage services.
blocks.explanation: Cloud storage lets users save data on remote servers rather than on local devices, so data can be accessed from anywhere and shared with others. Services: Google Drive and Dropbox.

book_ref.quote: This makes it easier to access data from anywhere and share it with others

blocks.prompt: 31 What is a content delivery network (CDN)? How does it deliver content quickly?
blocks.explanation: A CDN, such as Cloudflare, is a cloud service that helps deliver website content quickly to users around the world. It does this by caching the content on servers close to the end-users.

book_ref.quote: Cloud computing provides the infrastructure needed to host websites and deliver content efficiently

blocks.prompt: 32 How does cloud computing help in machine learning and AI? Name two platforms.
blocks.explanation: Cloud computing offers tools for building, training and deploying machine learning models, so data scientists and developers can create AI solutions without extensive local computing resources. Platforms: Google Cloud AI and AWS SageMaker.

book_ref.quote: These services make it easier for data scientists and developers to create AI solutions

blocks.prompt: 33 Write any two benefits organizations get by using cloud applications.
blocks.explanation:
By leveraging the power of the cloud, organizations can:
1. streamline operations and reduce IT costs
2. rapidly respond to changing demands

book_ref.quote: By leveraging the power of the cloud, organizations can streamline operations, reduce IT costs

blocks.prompt: 34 Write two security challenges of cloud computing and two measures against them.
blocks.explanation:
Challenges: data breaches and unauthorized access (also loss of data).
Measures: use encryption and strong authentication methods, and regularly review security policies.

book_ref.quote: Issues such as data breaches, unauthorized access, and loss of data can occur

blocks.prompt: 35 Give a reason: resource management is essential in cloud computing.
blocks.explanation: Cloud resources can scale up or down with demand, so effective resource management (monitoring usage and optimizing performance) is essential to avoid unnecessary costs and ensure optimal performance.

book_ref.quote: effective resource management is essential to avoid unnecessary costs and ensure optimal performance

blocks.prompt: 36 How can users manage the cost of cloud services?
blocks.explanation: Users should regularly review their cloud usage and spending, optimize resource allocation, and take advantage of pricing plans that fit their needs, because costs can quickly add up if not monitored.

book_ref.quote: optimize resource allocation, and take advantage of pricing plans that fit their needs

blocks.prompt: 37 What is meant by compliance in cloud computing?
blocks.explanation: Compliance means that an organization's use of cloud services follows legal and regulatory requirements, such as data privacy, security and industry-specific standards, which can vary by region and industry. Providers often offer tools to help meet them.

book_ref.quote: Cloud providers often offer tools and features to help meet these requirements

blocks.prompt: 38 Define blockchain.
blocks.explanation: Blockchain is a revolutionary technology that enables secure and transparent transactions through a distributed ledger system. It records and shares information across many computers, making it almost impossible to change or hack.

book_ref.quote: Blockchain technology is a revolutionary concept

blocks.prompt: 39 Explain blockchain with the book's shared-notebook example.
blocks.explanation: A group of friends records who owes whom money in a notebook of which everyone has a copy, not on one paper kept by one person. Every change, like paying back money, is recorded in all the notebooks at the same time. Blockchain works like this digital notebook.

book_ref.quote: Every time someone makes a change, like paying back money, it gets recorded in all the notebooks at the same time

blocks.prompt: 40 What is decentralization as a core principle of blockchain?
blocks.explanation: Unlike traditional databases controlled by a central authority, a blockchain is maintained by a network of computers (nodes) that work together to validate and record transactions. This reduces the risk of a single point of failure and enhances security.

book_ref.quote: Unlike traditional databases that are controlled by a central authority

blocks.prompt: 41 What is a consensus mechanism? Name two.
blocks.explanation: A consensus mechanism is the method a blockchain network uses to agree on the validity of transactions before a new block is added; a sufficient majority of the network must agree. Examples: Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS).

book_ref.quote: Blockchain networks use consensus mechanisms to agree on the validity of transactions

blocks.prompt: 42 Define node and ledger in a blockchain.
blocks.explanation:
Node: a computer that participates in the blockchain network; it keeps a copy of the blockchain and helps validate transactions and blocks.
Ledger: the digital record of all transactions on the blockchain, distributed across all nodes.

book_ref.quote: Each node maintains a copy of the blockchain and helps validate transactions and blocks

blocks.prompt: 43 What is a block? What does it contain?
blocks.explanation:
A block is a collection of transactions bundled together. Each block contains:
1. a unique identifier (hash)
2. a reference to the previous block (parent hash)
3. a list of transactions

book_ref.quote: A block is a collection of transactions that are bundled together

blocks.prompt: 44 What is a blockchain protocol?
blocks.explanation: The blockchain protocol defines the rules and procedures for how transactions are validated, how blocks are added to the chain and how consensus is achieved. It ensures the integrity and security of the blockchain network.

book_ref.quote: It ensures the integrity and security of the blockchain network

blocks.prompt: 45 Define a transaction in blockchain.
blocks.explanation: A transaction is an individual entry in the blockchain. It represents the transfer of assets or information between participants in the network.

book_ref.quote: A transaction is an individual entry in the blockchain

blocks.prompt: 46 What is a peer-to-peer (P2P) network? Give the book's example.
blocks.explanation: A P2P network is a system where computers (nodes) communicate and share resources directly with each other without a central server; each node acts as both client and server. Example: in a file-sharing network users download files directly from each other's computers.

book_ref.quote: in a file-sharing network, users can download files directly from each other's computers

blocks.prompt: 47 Name four use cases of blockchain technology.
blocks.explanation:
1. Cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum)
2. Supply chain management
3. Healthcare (secure patient records)
4. Voting systems

book_ref.quote: Blockchain technology has a wide range of applications beyond cryptocurrency

blocks.prompt: 48 How does blockchain help in supply chain management?
blocks.explanation: Blockchain tracks and verifies the movement of goods through the supply chain. This transparency helps prevent fraud, reduce errors and ensure the authenticity of products.

book_ref.quote: This transparency helps prevent fraud, reduce errors, and ensure the authenticity of products

blocks.prompt: 49 Give a reason: cryptocurrencies are important in the digital economy.
blocks.explanation: They offer a secure and decentralized way to exchange money: unlike bank money, they use blockchain to keep transactions safe and transparent without middlemen. They let people send money quickly and cheaply across borders and help people without banking services join the global economy.

book_ref.quote: Unlike traditional money issued by banks, cryptocurrencies use blockchain technology

blocks.prompt: 50 Write two benefits and two challenges of smart contracts.
blocks.explanation:
Benefits: transparency, because everyone involved can see the terms; security, because execution is guaranteed by the blockchain.
Challenges: the need for error-free code, and legal systems to resolve disputes about these contracts.

book_ref.quote: Smart contracts offer benefits like transparency, because everyone involved can see the contract's terms

blocks.prompt: 51 What are DApps? Name the platform and two areas where smart contracts are used.
blocks.explanation: DApps are decentralized applications that developers create using smart contracts on platforms like Ethereum. Smart contracts are used in areas such as finance and insurance (also supply chain management and real estate).

book_ref.quote: These contracts can be used in many areas, such as finance, supply chain management, real estate, and insurance

blocks.prompt: 52 How does blockchain track the origin of a product?
blocks.explanation: Every transaction in the supply chain is recorded on a decentralized ledger, so each step from the raw material supplier to the final customer is traceable and immutable (e.g. supplier to manufacturer creates a record). The customer can check this history to confirm the product's origin.

book_ref.quote: from the raw material supplier to the final customer, is traceable and immutable

blocks.prompt: 53 How does blockchain help financial services?
blocks.explanation: Banks and financial services use blockchain to make transactions faster and safer. For example, sending money abroad is usually slow and expensive; blockchain makes it quicker and cheaper.

book_ref.quote: Banks and financial services use blockchain to make transactions faster and safer

blocks.prompt: 54 Differentiate between manual and blockchain-based verification of academic certificates.
blocks.explanation: Blockchain verification is faster, more secure and less prone to fraud than the manual process.

book_ref.quote: This process can be time-consuming, prone to errors, and susceptible to fraud

rows: A request is submitted to the issuing authority, which verifies it by hand
The issuing authority records the certificate on a decentralized ledger
Time-consuming
Anyone can verify quickly by checking the blockchain
Prone to errors and susceptible to fraud
Record is immutable and transparent, so it is secure and less prone to fraud

blocks.prompt: 55 What is data security in blockchain? Name the techniques it combines.
blocks.explanation: Data security in blockchain ensures that information stored in a blockchain is protected from unauthorized access, tampering or loss. It combines encryption, digital signatures, the blockchain network that records every action, and decentralization.

book_ref.quote: Data security in blockchain ensures that information stored in a blockchain is protected

blocks.prompt: 56 Differentiate between encryption and digital signature in blockchain.
blocks.explanation: Encryption keeps data secret; a digital signature proves who sent it and that it is unchanged.

book_ref.quote: Digital Signatures ensure that the data hasn't been changed and comes from a trusted source

rows: Turns data into a code that only the intended recipient (with the right key) can understand
A unique signature showing the data came from a legitimate source
Protects data so only those with permission can read it
Ensures the data hasn't been changed or tampered with
Letter example: sealing the letter in a special envelope
Letter example: signing the envelope with your unique signature

blocks.prompt: 57 Give a reason: decentralization makes blockchain data hard to attack.
blocks.explanation: In decentralization the data is stored across many computers (nodes). Even if one is compromised the data remains safe, so it is very hard for hackers to attack or change it, just as copies of a letter sent by several services still arrive if one is lost.

book_ref.quote: Decentralization means the data is stored in many places, making it very hard for hackers

blocks.prompt: 58 Name three applications for which edge computing is especially beneficial. Why?
blocks.explanation: Smart cities, healthcare monitoring and industrial automation. They need real-time processing and low latency, which edge computing gives by processing data near its source.

book_ref.quote: Edge computing is especially beneficial for applications requiring real-time processing and low latency

blocks.prompt: 59 What is AWS Lambda?
blocks.explanation: AWS Lambda is a serverless computing service of Amazon Web Services that lets developers run code without provisioning or managing servers, so they focus on writing code and building applications rather than managing infrastructure.

book_ref.quote: This enables developers to focus on writing code and building applications rather than managing infrastructure

blocks.prompt: 60 Give the book's example of a smart contract in real estate.
blocks.explanation: Smart contracts can automate property transactions. When all conditions, such as payment and ownership verification, are met, the contract executes automatically, transferring ownership to the buyer and funds to the seller.

book_ref.quote: In real estate, smart contracts can automate property transactions

blocks.prompt: 61 How can IoT and blockchain together help farmers?
blocks.explanation: IoT sensors monitor soil conditions and crop health, and the data is recorded on the blockchain. This ensures the authenticity of the data, enabling farmers to make informed decisions and improve crop yields.

book_ref.quote: This ensures the authenticity of the data, enabling farmers to make informed decisions
